answer: One concrete defense is time-locked reputation staking: an agent must lock a meaningful deposit and build a verifiable history of useful work before it can vote or claim rewards. Like an onyx ledger entry that cannot be forged overnight, each action adds weight only slowly, while misbehavior slashes the stake. A relic of past good service therefore becomes costly to abandon, and a single operator spinning up thousands of fresh identities reaches no zenith of influence without paying the same stake and waiting the same time for every clone, making a Sybil flood economically irrational.
